# Daemon, setup and plumbing (area `daemon`)

The background service, its RPC areas, setup/install/update commands, device facts, permissions, traces, failure-report relay.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **DMN-1** (owner): `ferb chat` and its live renderer are gone, with the dead `questions.answer` loop. Voice and any text that pointed to "ferb chat's hidden prompt" point to the app. `task.stop` requires task ids (the app sends them); stopping everything is the separate global stop (`stop.engage`).
- **DMN-3** (owner): The `ferb` program is only invisible plumbing (the `setup` commands the app calls, `mcp` for the models' tool bridge, `daemon run`) plus a developer toolbox (trace, logs, stats, doctor, memory, restore, ps, verdict, runtimes, browsers) used to debug and never presented to users. All user commands go; push-to-talk and identity-profile setup live in the app.
- **DMN-4** (owner): The Mac probe and watch harness, the CLI permission walkthrough (the app does it), the old chat renderer, the duplicate trace renderer and the dormant conversations / notifications / test-mode commands are removed. Kept: trace, logs, stats, doctor, memory, restore, ps, setup/uninstall, verdict, runtimes, browsers, mcp.
- **DMN-5** (owner): FERB samples the screen state before and after tools that can change the owner's screen (Mac input, foreground, opening an app), never around read-only tools and never by polling. It ignores the owner's own cursor moves, records only changes FERB could have caused (front app, focus, Space, fullscreen) and gives them to the merged checker as facts about how the work was done.
- **DMN-6** (owner): FERB has a read-only self-description built from code and config so it never goes stale: version, models per role, permissions, current settings, what it records about the owner, where and for how long (from the retention rules), health and cost. A short summary is in every prompt; the full detail comes through a worker lookup tool. App how-tos come from a list kept with the UI. Settings stay the owner's to change in the app; FERB says where.
- **DMN-7** (owner): When asked, FERB may talk about its models, its settings and how it works.
- **DMN-8** (owner): Failure reports and diagnostic files become issues in the private GitHub repo Json604/ferb-reports through a relay the owner owns (a Cloudflare Worker holding a fine-grained token limited to that repo's Issues and Contents, read and write). The user only presses Send in FERB: no GitHub account, browser, Mail app or extra step; they still preview the cleaned report first.
- **DMN-9** (owner): Each Send files exactly one issue with a short summary (what failed, the errors and questions, FERB's version, the report id) linking the full redacted report, stored as one file in the repo (reports/YYYY/MM/<report id>….txt); no reply-comment threads. A report over 25 MB is shortened by FERB to fit (summary, every error and question and the last part of the trace kept; what was cut stated at the top); the full report stays on the Mac.
- **DMN-10** (owner): A reinstall over an older FERB's leftover files proceeds normally when nothing is broken. FERB's program files and own state are recreated; the owner's data that can't be read is moved aside with a timestamp (never deleted) and the owner is told once (STORE-1, STORE-2); a database from a newer FERB is not broken (STORE-3).
- **DMN-11** (agent): The daemon builds its stores first, then hands the gateway one GatewayDeps (standing permissions included) and the supervisor typed ports (memory, schedules, environment, desktop, browser, notify) plus a QuestionRouter. Every field is required and missing wiring fails at construction; no hooks are set afterwards. The supervisor's observer and conversation guard reach the gateway through one Gateway.attach call.
- **DMN-12** (agent): Config is parsed once and parsed again only when the file (or its owner or mode) changes. A setting changed in the app, privacy exclusions included, reaches the Redactor, the proxy and hearing at once, without a restart.
- **DMN-13** (agent): Blocking calls (codesign, the sandbox check, profile discovery, TCC checks, image work) run in worker threads. The retention pass reads what to delete in a worker thread on a read-only connection, then deletes on the loop's connection 200 rows a transaction, leaving the loop free between batches.
- **DMN-14** (agent): Every daemon and native-host launch runs Python with -P (never prepend the working directory) and FERB's home as the working folder. FERB.app's definition runs the agent with exactly -m ferb.daemon; the daemon makes FERB's home its working folder and sends output launchd left at /dev/null to logs/daemon.{out,err}.log.
- **DMN-18** (agent): A checkout install builds ~/.ferb/venv.new (uv venv --relocatable; uv export --frozen, then uv pip install --require-hashes; FERB with --no-deps), the secret helper and Codex (npm ci from package-lock.json) beside the old ones, and swaps them in only with the daemon stopped (a cut-off swap is finished next time). Any failure leaves the venv, plist and running daemon untouched.
- **DMN-19** (agent): Codex is (re)installed only when a role uses it (Codex when unset) or when the owner signs in to it (--codex-login installs it first); a link into FERB.app follows the same rule.
- **DMN-20** (agent): Only `ferb uninstall --purge` (the owner typed delete, or answered FERB.app's one question) deletes every item of FERB's Keychain services (ferb, ferb.owner-secrets, Claude Code's item for FERB's Claude home) with security delete-generic-password -s SERVICE, repeated until none is left (at most 10,000). FERB never lists or reads a value.

- **DMN-28** (agent): reports.build writes the redacted file; the app shows View report and Send. reports.send takes only a regular file named like a report directly in ~/.ferb/reports (no symlink, O_NOFOLLOW), passes it through the Redactor's text pass again and rewrites the saved file to match, so what is kept is what was sent. - **DMN-30** (agent): POST /file carries GitHub's exact create-file JSON built by FERB; the Worker checks headers, query and rate limit, picks reports/YYYY/MM/<id>-<8 random>.txt, streams the body to the Contents API and returns a signed 1-hour ticket (409 retry on a commit conflict). - **DMN-403** (agent): A preview capture takes the surface's resource locks only when they are free (`try_hold`, no yield between the look and the take; a lock just handed to a waking worker counts as busy); busy, it returns the cached last frame with a state. Limits unchanged.

- **DMN-556** (agent): For APP-805 and APP-806. chat.history.page {day, before?, limit? (30, at most 200), open?} gives the day's newest entries before the cursor, oldest first, with more, cursor (the oldest's at|id) and context (turns its replies answer that aren't on it); open adds every turn still waiting for FERB's answer. chat.history.days {} lists the days, newest first. A notice whose ref is one of attention_notices says that record's text and quotes, and attention.expire_derived (a forget, the typed-text purge) clears it in chat_history too.
- **DMN-580** (agent): Keeps DMN-551. runtimes.status adds per runtime effort and refused {account, at, fix} (journal runtime.signed_out / usage_limit / answered, never cleared by the presence check) and role_details {role: runtime, model, effort}. runtimes.models adds effort, levels, default_efforts. runtimes.model takes effort ("" clears, absent keeps). runtimes.changed (critical bus) on a role, model, effort, key, sign-in or refusal change. setup.browsers rows add version, too_old, problem. Worker port runtime_account(name, account).
- **DMN-581** (owner): Nothing shows test mode in Settings; test mode itself is removed completely. Its removal is its own job (T-1080), not part of the Settings fix.
- **DMN-582** (agent): For DMN-581. FERB has no test.mode RPC, no saved [test_mode] state, no test-mode send allowlist and no record mode (FERB's questions answered from a fixed table). Every question reaches the owner as in normal use; sends are guarded by the sink rule and the confirmations. A config that still holds test_mode.state, on or off, starts with test mode gone: the key is removed once and journaled (config.upgraded); an older caller of test.mode gets the unknown-method refusal. In a developer run the owner answers (RUN-442's no payment); the run tool is GATE-577.
- **DMN-583** (agent): For ORCH-591. question.asked also stores the question's first line (its summary, else its text) and its exact part's, at most 200 characters each; question.answered stores a typed answer's first line (`said`, 200) unless the card is a hidden input (code, secret, password) or FERB hid a secret in the answer. The journal redacts both as it redacts everything. Never a payment's picture (GATE-579). Older rows without them read as before.
- **DMN-584** (agent): For APP-888, refining DMN-403. A task still captures one surface at a time. A request for another step's surface while a capture runs answers busy at once with its last frame and is remembered; when the capture ends, that surface goes next (a request for any other surface answers busy until it comes, at most TURN_S, 1 s, after it was turned away; the app asks again 200 ms after a busy answer). Requests for the surface being captured share it. No frame-rate cap (APP-405).
- **DMN-585** (agent): Refines DMN-26. A thread that services its own run loop does it only through autorelease.native_loop: each turn runs the thread's step (the Accessibility watcher's app listing, presence's read) and the run-loop slice that dispatches its callbacks in one pool. The Accessibility, workspace and presence watchers, the owner-input tap, FSEvents and the self-test tap use it. Each native callback's body runs in a pool too. Elsewhere only one zero-wait turn inside a pool (_macos_events, the disturbance probe's pump).
- **DMN-586** (agent): For L12 and ORCH-637. A capture at send first reads the window list, then finds the app that sent the message (the sending CLI's host) and picks the window, in one step on FRONT_WINDOW_CHOOSER (two threads of its own), never queued behind other work in the loop's shared pool. A capture stopped during that step is journaled as screen.capture_stalled with the step "windows".
- **DMN-587** (owner): Refines DMN-513 ("SMAppService returns with the Developer ID"). A FERB.app signed with the Developer ID registers the daemon's definition inside the app with SMAppService. Today's user LaunchAgent stays as an automatic fallback, so FERB keeps running when the registration doesn't work. A self-signed or ad-hoc FERB.app keeps the LaunchAgent (DMN-513).
- **DMN-588** (owner): When the installed FERB.app is signed with a certificate, the APP_ONLY check accepts only a peer signed with FERB's release certificate (its leaf in scripts/release-cert.sha1) or FERB's Developer ID team (scripts/developer-team.txt) while the switch release ships, then only the team. Ad-hoc development builds stay unpinned.
- **DMN-589** (agent): For DMN-587. service.json records `signer` (team:<ID>, leaf:<SHA-1> or adhoc, from codesign) and `service` (app or launch_agent; a LaunchAgent's sha256 only for launch_agent). `setup --service [--update] --app-service` installs as before, then boots out a running LaunchAgent, waits for its process, deletes the plist and loads nothing (a registration launchd already runs is kickstarted -k). With service = app the clean-up stops the daemon with launchctl kill SIGTERM and starts it with kickstart, never unregistering it; the daemon puts back no plist.
- **DMN-590** (agent): Setup writes the new ferb-secrets and its .requirement whole as staged files first; only then are both renamed into place, one right after the other. A failure while writing either (a full disk, a quit) leaves the helper in use with its own pin and removes the staged files.
- **DMN-592** (agent): Beyond DMN-14's redirect, the Rust daemon writes timestamped, redacted lines to stderr (logs/daemon.err.log under launchd): its start (pid, version, build, who started it), when its socket serves and when every call is answered (ms since the process started) with slow steps' durations, its stop, FERB.app-only verdicts (the first app accepted, every caller refused), each bounded journal problem (_Repeats, e.g. browser.connection_refused), and a panic with place, redacted message and backtrace, journaled daemon.unhandled.
- **DMN-593** (owner): FERB's Rust build, signed with the Developer ID, registers its background service through the app (SMAppService) and in no other way: no LaunchAgent fallback with the same label, and no code that moves a self-signed install's service, login item or permission entries. When macOS refuses the registration, FERB says why and how to allow it. An update from one Developer ID build to the next keeps the service and the permissions. For the Rust build this takes the place of DMN-587's fallback and of APP-902, APP-904 and APP-905.
- **DMN-594** (agent): For DMN-593. A packaged FERB.app with no Python inside (the Rust build) registers its own service whoever signed it, ad-hoc too: from FERB.app the Rust installer is always the app's service (Installer::in_app; service = app, a LaunchAgent found retired, nothing loaded). Without a Team ID it registers afresh at each setup (APP-599). A restart only kickstarts. A job launchd can't start is registered again once; then, or on a refusal or 30 s of silence, the service line says why and to check Login Items, with Try again. The Python build keeps its LaunchAgent.
